paper: Cengiz, Dube, Lindner, Zipperer (2019), 'The Effect of Minimum Wages on Low-Wage Jobs', QJE 134(3):1405-1454.
global_note: The original toolchain is Stata (reghdfe/estout/ftools/gtools/moremata) -- proprietary, license-gated, and NOT installable without a paid license (verified: no stata binary/license present; apt/pip/conda cannot provide it). Rather than stop, the entire estimation pipeline was faithfully ported to R: reghdfe -> fixest::feols (identical HDFE + cluster-robust VCE), and the custom Stata programs (treatmentdefinition/abovebelowbunch/lincomestadd/nlcomestadd/Table_create/makefigure_massovertime, incl. the wage-bill 'no-spillover' method) reimplemented as R functions with delta-method SEs (numDeriv). All derived .dta inputs were present, so master_QJE.do's data-creation block was correctly skipped (as the plan specifies). All reported numbers are what the R port actually produced.

fixes_applied.diff_snippet: reghdfe Y treat, absorb(i.wagebinstate i.wagequarterdate ...) cluster(statenum) [aw=wt]  ==>  feols(Y ~ treat | wagebinstate + wagequarterdate + factor(postcont_m)+..., weights=~wt, cluster=~statenum)

step_outcomes.notes: The treatment/window/control dummies are precomputed columns in the primary .dta (treatmentdefinition's primary branch only loads data), so the treatment design needed no reconstruction. reghdfe absorb() semantics ported faithfully: bare categorical controls (postcont_*, controlf) -> factor() FE; i.one#c.var linear controls (window, before/after treats) -> ordinary RHS regressors (FWL-equivalent for reported treat coefs).

step_outcomes.description: Table 4: total %dW affected wage, no-spillover counterfactual, spillover share (overall, demographic subgroups, incumbents m1 / new entrants m2).
step_outcomes.command_executed: Rscript rport/groups.R ; Rscript rport/figure4.R (m1/m2) ; finalize -> Table4.tex
step_outcomes.stdout: overall spillover=0.397; incumbent(m1) %dW=0.067 spillover=0.511; new-entrant(m2) %dW=0.042 spillover=0.073.
step_outcomes.notes: Overall: %dW affected wage=0.068, no-spillover=0.041, spillover share=0.397 (~40%, matches paper). Demographic spillover shares 0.35-0.40 (BH 0.18). Incumbents (m1) vs new entrants (m2): affected-wage change 0.067 vs 0.042, spillover share 0.511 vs 0.073 -- spillovers accrue mostly to incumbents, as in the paper. The 'no-spillover' wage effect is a linear combo of the below-MW (missing-jobs) coefficients (-sum_j j*b[treat_m_j])*0.8/EWB; spillover=1-noSpill/total via delta method.

step_outcomes.notes: Incumbents: Delta_b=-0.009 (0.002), Delta_a=0.011 (0.002), %dEmp=0.038, %dWage=0.067, spillover=0.511. New entrants: Delta_b=-0.004, Delta_a=0.005, %dEmp=0.024, %dWage=0.042, spillover=0.073. Both show missing-below ~= excess-above (net employment ~0); incumbents get larger wage gains and much higher spillover than new entrants -- the paper's qualitative result. Directionally and roughly matches the paper's annotated values (incumbent Da=0.014/Db=-0.013/%dW=0.095; new entrant Da=0.006/Db=-0.005/%dW=0.019). SCOPE NOTE (labeled deviation): estimated on the core -4..+4 window with Table-1-style controls; the paper's placebo far-above controls (placebocontafter1/2, windowpl1/2) and +5..+17 bins were omitted (they need treat_p8..p17 not shipped as columns), which shifts the incumbent magnitudes slightly toward zero.

step_outcomes.description: Figure 5: total/missing/excess employment change vs minimum-to-median (Kaitz) wage ratio across events.
step_outcomes.stdout: slopes vs Kaitz ratio -- total emp 0.006 (0.039); missing -0.133 (0.032); excess 0.139 (0.046).
step_outcomes.notes: Uses precomputed event-specific estimates (stacked_events_new_event_specific_estimates_clean_controls.dta). Total-employment slope vs Kaitz ratio = 0.006 (0.039) -- essentially flat; missing-jobs slope = -0.133 (0.032) and excess-jobs slope = +0.139 (0.046) both scale with how binding the MW is and cancel. Exactly the paper's Figure 5 message. Robust (HC) OLS, weighted, DC excluded; binscatter emulated by residualizing on controls (unemp_rate, urbanshare, decade dummies, republican) and decile-binning.

step_outcomes.description: Figure 6 / A11: classic TWFE-logMW aggregate employment elasticity + wage-bin decomposition.
step_outcomes.stdout: Aggregate employment elasticity w.r.t. MW = -0.089 (0.025), 95% CI [-0.140,-0.039].
step_outcomes.notes: Aggregate TWFE-logMW employment elasticity = -0.089 (0.025). Bin decomposition (Figure6.pdf) shows sizeable negative contributions in high wage bins ($6-$9 and $15-$19) far above the new MW where a causal MW effect is implausible -- the paper's demonstration that the canonical negative elasticity is spuriously spread across the wage distribution. Uses state-year panel, F2/F1/L0..L4 log-MW, state & year FE, weighted by avg population, clustered by state; aggregate = average cumulative effect over 5 horizons / mean E-pop.
